candidates: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:482 - isAccessTokenId never actually checks the grant shortcut. The grant shortcut sits at index 4–5 of the 6-character prefix, but the code reads `substring(3, 5)`. For `onrtac` that gives `ta`. The condition is also inverted: it returns false when the value *matches* the expected shortcut. Because the offset is wrong, the comparison never matches, so the matcher accepts any `xxxxxx:<uuid>` token ID no matter the grant type. The tests that use it (code-to-token, refresh, device, CIBA) can't catch a wrong or missing grant type. Fix: `if (items[0].length() != 6 || !items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 - Null check for rawTokenId tests grantType instead. `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks `grantType` a second time, so a null `rawTokenId` is accepted. Encoding then produces an ID ending in `:null`. Change it to `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.
